description: Maps issuer names as they appear in Vanguard 500 Index Fund Schedules of Investments to the ticker this repository prices them under. Derived from data/raw/ground_truth/vanguard_audited_rosters.json; covers every issuer reaching a Top 20 between 1994 and 2006.
why: Filed issuer names are not stable. A registrant is renamed (Philip Morris to Altria, SBC to AT&T Inc.), merges under a new name (Exxon to ExxonMobil, Citicorp to Citigroup), or is punctuated differently between filings. Matching on the name alone therefore splits one issuer into several or conflates two, and both errors are silent.
ticker_choice: Where a rename leaves the same registrant continuing, both names map to the ticker whose price series covers the whole period. Where two distinct registrants combine, the surviving ticker carries the series from the merger onward and the predecessor is priced separately up to it.

continuations.MO: Philip Morris Cos. renamed itself Altria Group in 2003; one registrant, one series.
continuations.VZ: Bell Atlantic renamed itself Verizon Communications in 2000 on merging with GTE. Bell Atlantic is the continuing registrant, so its pre-2000 years are priced as VZ; GTE is priced separately as its own registrant up to its 1999 year end.
continuations.XOM: Exxon Corp. is the continuing registrant after the 1999 Mobil merger. Mobil is priced separately as MOB up to its 1998 year end.
continuations.C: Citicorp combined with Travelers to form Citigroup in 1998. The repository prices the combined entity as C throughout.
continuations.BAC: BankAmerica Corp. became Bank of America Corp.; one registrant, one series.
continuations.T: SBC Communications acquired AT&T Corp. in 2005 and adopted the AT&T Inc. name. SBC is priced as SBC up to its 2004 year end and as T from 2005; the separate Ma Bell registrant is T_CORP.

not_matched_deliberately.# Microsoft Corp: A stray footnote marker on the 1996 filing's Microsoft row. Normalisation strips leading markers, so this resolves to Microsoft Corp rather than being mapped separately.
not_matched_deliberately.AT&T: Denotes two registrants. SEI writes it for AT&T Corp through its 2005 schedule, alongside a separate SBC Communications line; SBC renamed itself AT&T Inc. in November 2005, so from the 2006 schedule the same string means the registrant this repository prices as T. Resolved by period in derive_quarterly_constituent_series.py rather than mapped here, because a name-to-ticker entry cannot express the change and would extend T_CORP a year past Ma Bell's existence. See 4.5.
not_matched_deliberately.AT&T Wireless Services: The 2001 spinoff, a separate registrant from AT&T Corp. Not priced by this repository; mapping it to T_CORP would merge two issuers held in the same filing.
not_matched_deliberately.MCI Communications: The predecessor registrant acquired by WorldCom in September 1998. ticker_choice prices a predecessor separately up to a combination rather than folding it into the survivor, so it is not mapped to MCIC.
not_matched_deliberately.Viacom Inc: Prudential lists one Viacom line with no share class stated. Class A is left unmapped deliberately (see share_classes), so an unclassed line cannot be assumed to be Class B. SEI names the class explicitly and supplies these periods instead.
not_matched_deliberately.Tyco Electronics, Ltd: Spun off from Tyco International in 2007 and listed separately from it in the same SPY filings. A distinct registrant, not priced here.

below_top20: Entries beyond the Top 20 are included where the constituent is required elsewhere: a name absent from every Top 20 still needs a price when a portfolio holds it into a later year, and the gap report (universe_gap_report.json) reaches rank 30.
share_classes: Viacom listed Class A and Class B separately at different prices. Only Class B is mapped, following the single-line dual-class execution convention established for Alphabet in #38 and documented in docs/DATA_PROVENANCE.md 4.3.8. Class A is left unmapped deliberately so it cannot be conflated with Class B. SPY's unclassed "Viacom, Inc" line (1997-2004) IS mapped to Class B, on evidence rather than assumption: that trust lists exactly ONE Viacom line in every filing from 1997 to 2009, and from 2005 it labels that same line Class B, with the share count running continuously across the change. Prudential's unclassed "Viacom Inc" is NOT mapped, because nothing in its own filings identifies the class and SEI names the class explicitly for the same periods.
